title: Hardwired LED Ceiling Light: Wiring a New Fixture with a Wall Switch
summary: This Old House's Ask This Old House episode demonstrates upgrading a ceiling lighting situation by replacing a cord-hung fixture with a hardwired LED fixture controlled from a wall switch. The crew identifies hazards of the old setup, plans a new ceiling box and a switch location, routes power from a convenient junction box to the wall switch, and then from the switch to the ceiling fixture. They pull wires with fish tape, splice neutrals, connect hot to the switch, and bond the ground, using Madison bars to secure boxes. The LED fixture is described as having a driver that converts house power to low voltage, producing bright light at a low 18-watt consumption, and weighs about two pounds. The result is a flush-mounted, switch-controlled ceiling light that eliminates the prior hanging hazard and makes the room feel larger.
topics: safety hazards of exposed fixture wiring
fixture mounting hardware and ceiling box alignment
wire routing from junction box to switch to fixture

sections.title: Assess old fixture and safety hazard
sections.description: Introduction to the current fixture and its risks (lamp cord across the ceiling and down the wall); recognition that the existing setup is a pulling hazard and can cause electric shock if prongs are touched.

sections.title: LED fixture introduction and power characteristics
sections.description: Announcement of a slim, LED-based fixture that uses LEDs with a driver to convert power; emphasis on bright output with only 18 watts of electricity.

sections.title: Plan ceiling box location and switch height
sections.description: Decision to install a ceiling fixture box in the prior fixture location; plan for switch placement on the wall and set switch height at 48 inches to center.

sections.title: Power routing plan
sections.description: Proposed routing: power comes from a nearby junction box, goes to the light switch, then returns across the ceiling to the new fixture location.

sections.title: Fish tape prep and feed to the work area
concepts: pulling wires through walls and ceiling
sections.description: Preparation and use of fish tape to establish a pull path from the fixture to the switch location for wiring access.

sections.title: Switch wiring and understanding toggle switch
sections.description: Explanation of a two-wire switch loop: neutrals spliced, hot and switched hot wired to the switch, and a demonstration of how a toggle switch passes or breaks power.

sections.title: Securing boxes with Madison bars and wall finishing
sections.description: Demonstration of using Madison bars to anchor the box to the framing, then securing and finishing the wall around the new box.

sections.title: Run, install, and test the fixture with LED driver
sections.description: Finish wiring path to the ceiling fixture, discuss the LED driver’s role, mount the fixture, restore power, and test the new wall switch—resulting in a flush, hazard-free installation that enhances room feel.

featured_techniques.technique: Pull wires through ceiling and wall using fish tape
Use Madison bars to secure electrical boxes in wall/ceiling
Create a switch loop: splice neutrals, connect hot to switch, return switched hot to fixture
Route power from junction box to switch, then to fixture
Explain LED driver and low-wattage performance
